title: A Bi-Directional Dual-Path Boost-48V-Buck Hybrid Converter for High-Voltage Power-Transmission Cable in Light-Weight Humanoid Robots
problem: Humanoid robots with distributed actuators consume most energy in limbs while battery is centralized in torso, requiring high-current transmission through thick heavy cables causing large I²R losses.
method: Bi-directional dual-path boost-48V-buck hybrid converter stepping voltage up for efficient transmission to limbs and down for motor actuation, with separate boost and buck paths optimized for each direction.

title: Reproducibility Report for SC25 Paper RAPTOR: Practical Numerical Profiling of Scientific Applications
problem: Artifact evaluation and reproducibility assessment of RAPTOR numerical profiling framework
method: Systematic artifact evaluation following SC25 Reproducibility Initiative appendix requirements; reproducibility assessment of RAPTOR implementation

title: CTXNL: A Software-Hardware Co-designed Solution for Efficient CXL-Based Transaction Processing
problem: Directly adopting CXL for multi-node transaction processing incurs high performance overhead because standard CXL cache coherence primitives enforce fine-grained coherence uniformly, while transactional data has loosely coherent access patterns that do not require full coherence at every access.
method: CTXNL is a software-hardware co-designed system that introduces a hybrid coherence primitive tailored to the transactional access pattern. The core mechanism allows transaction developers to selectively opt in or out of cache coherence on a per-data-item basis, bypassing full CXL coherence overhead for data items that are only loosely coherent during normal transaction execution while maintaining correctness via selective coherence enforcement at commit or conflict points. Hardware support is added to CXL memory controllers to efficiently implement the selective coherence primitive.

title: SpecASan: Mitigating Transient Execution Attacks Using Speculative Address Sanitization
problem: Transient execution attacks (Spectre, Meltdown, MDS) exploit speculative execution to leak sensitive data through residual microarchitectural state, and existing defenses either delay speculative execution or require costly shadow structures and dynamic information flow tracking. Providing strong security against transient execution attacks without significant performance overhead remains an open problem.
method: SpecASan extends ARM's Memory Tagging Extension (MTE) from the committed path to the speculative path. When a speculative memory access fails the MTE tag comparison (i.e., the tag on the pointer does not match the tag in memory), that access is stalled until speculation resolves, preventing it from affecting microarchitectural state (caches, TLBs). This is combined with existing Control-Flow Integrity (CFI) enforcement to block gadget construction. The approach models transient execution attacks as software-defined security contract violations and enforces the contracts in hardware using existing MTE tag-check hardware, requiring minimal new hardware.

title: OctoCache: Caching Voxels for Accelerating 3D Occupancy Mapping in Autonomous Systems
problem: OctoMap, a widely used octree-based 3D mapping framework for autonomous robots, suffers from slow update performance due to costly and irregular memory accesses into the octree structure. The lack of cache-friendly access patterns and parallelism limits real-time deployment on autonomous platforms such as UAVs.
method: OctoCache is a software-level acceleration system with three techniques: (1) optimized cache memory access patterns that restructure octree node traversal to improve spatial locality, (2) refined voxel ordering that reorders ray-casting updates to maximize cache reuse, and (3) workflow parallelization that concurrently executes independent map-update tasks. No custom hardware is introduced; the system targets general-purpose CPUs.

title: lsCOMP: Efficient Light Source Compression
problem: Light source facilities generate X-ray data at 250 GB/s currently, projected to exceed 1 TB/s by end of decade. Intense data streams create critical I/O and bandwidth bottlenecks for data offload to HPC systems. Local processing capacity insufficient for online analysis.
method: lsCOMP single-kernel GPU compressor supporting both lossless and configurable lossy modes: (1) Single kernel design for streamlined implementation, (2) High compression throughput (380-509 GB/s lossless), (3) Flexible precision control for lossy compression, (4) Support for diverse light source data types, (5) TB/s-level random access throughput.

title: AnyKey: A Key-Value SSD for All Workload Types
problem: Existing Key-Value SSD (KV-SSD) designs are optimized only for workloads where values are much larger than keys; when key sizes are relatively large (an unexplored but real workload class), the expanded key metadata causes significantly degraded performance and potentially unbounded metadata growth.
method: AnyKey redesigns the KV-SSD metadata management architecture to prevent metadata size from scaling with key size. It introduces a metadata-bounded key representation that separates key identity from the full key payload, storing only fixed-size key references (hashes or compact descriptors) in the primary metadata structures while managing full key payloads separately. This ensures metadata overhead remains bounded regardless of key size distribution.

title: BOSS: Blocking algorithm for optimizing shuttling scheduling in Ion Trap
problem: Shuttling operations in ion trap quantum computers cause significant fidelity loss and elongated execution times, particularly as circuit sizes grow to 4000+ two-qubit gates across 64-78 qubits.
method: BOSS is a blocking algorithm that groups quantum operations into blocks to reduce the total number of shuttle operations required during circuit execution. The algorithm is evaluated on realistic experimental parameters incorporating sympathetic cooling for higher fidelity and more accurate execution time estimation. Experiments cover circuits with up to 4000+ two-qubit gates and 64-78 qubits.

title: PracMHBench: Re-evaluating Model-Heterogeneous Federated Learning Based on Practical Edge Device Constraints
problem: Model-heterogeneous federated learning (allowing different model architectures per device) is more practical than homogeneous FL, but existing algorithms have not been rigorously evaluated against real edge device constraints and resource limitations.
method: PracMHBench constructs a system platform to evaluate model-heterogeneous FL algorithms under practical edge device constraints, classifying diverse heterogeneity algorithms and testing on multiple data tasks and resource constraint scenarios.

title: Efficient Mitigation of DRAM Row Buffer Conflict Using Request Clustering in Manycore Systems
problem: Memory wall: DRAM row buffer conflicts cause inefficient bandwidth utilization in manycore systems
method: Request clustering to mitigate row buffer conflicts in manycore DRAM controllers

title: Concord: Rethinking Distributed Coherence for Software Caches in Serverless Environments
problem: Serverless functions incur high latency from frequent global storage accesses; existing node-local caching schemes either restrict each data item to a single cache node (causing frequent remote reads) or allow multi-node replication but impose heavy coherence overhead, neither being optimal for serverless access patterns characterized by frequent reads, strong temporal locality, and few concurrent writers.
method: Concord implements a directory-based distributed software cache coherence protocol inspired by hardware cache coherence, adapted for serverless environments. It allows multiple replicas of the same data item across nodes and satisfies reads locally from any replica. To maintain coherence, a directory tracks replica locations and manages invalidation/update messages on writes. The protocol minimizes coherence traffic by exploiting serverless access patterns, reduces contention points in the directory, and handles node failures and frequent coherence domain changes (as serverless function instances spin up/down). Two additional capabilities are unlocked: transactional storage accesses and transparent data-aware function placement.

title: COSMOS: Performance Portable Graph Pattern Matching with Domain-Specific Software Distributed Shared Memory
problem: Graph pattern matching (GPM) is NP-complete and irregular in nature, making it difficult to scale to distributed systems on complex supercomputers. Architecture-specific optimizations lack portability and cause vendor lock-in.
method: Domain-specific software distributed shared memory (DSM) model that abstracts supercomputer architecture diversity from users and developers, enabling portable parallel code execution.

title: A Single-Inductor-Based High-Voltage Transmit Beamformer for Wearable Ultrasound Devices Achieving 88% fCV2 Power Reduction
problem: Wearable ultrasound transducer arrays for vagus nerve stimulation suffer from excessive power loss from charging/discharging transducer capacitance (fCV² loss); prior resonant pulsers require multiple off-chip inductors, incompatible with miniaturized form factors.
method: A single-inductor resonant transmit beamformer architecture pulses groups of transducer elements at different phases from a shared inductor, enabling energy recycling across the array while avoiding the complex body-diode losses of prior approaches.

title: H2-LLM: Hardware-Dataflow Co-Exploration for Heterogeneous Hybrid-Bonding-based Low-Batch LLM Inference
problem: Edge-side low-batch LLM inference (personal assistant, reception bot, private edge server) is bottlenecked by the DRAM bandwidth wall: existing NMP designs embed compute engines inside DRAM dies, limiting compute capacity and creating an imbalance between bandwidth and computation for both prefill (compute-bound) and decoding (bandwidth-bound) stages. Hybrid-bonding technology offers a path to higher compute capacity near memory, but the trade-off between computation capacity and bandwidth has not been systematically explored.
method: H2-LLM proposes a hybrid-bonding-based heterogeneous accelerator that places high-capacity compute dies in face-to-face contact with DRAM dies, exploiting the high through-silicon-via bandwidth of hybrid bonding. The architecture exposes a design space covering compute tile counts, memory bandwidth allocation, and die partitioning. A data-centric dataflow abstraction is introduced to map LLM operations (attention, feed-forward, KV-cache access) onto the heterogeneous on-die and near-die compute resources across both prefill and decoding stages. A design space exploration (DSE) framework automatically searches this joint architecture-dataflow space for the Pareto-optimal configuration.

title: Effective Node-Level Anomaly Detection in HPC Systems via Coarse-Grained Clustering and Fine-Grained Model Sharing
problem: Large-scale HPC systems experience performance degradation and failures; anomaly detection at node-level is challenged by massive scales, frequent job transitions, and complex patterns.
method: NodeSentry: unsupervised framework combining coarse-grained clustering and fine-grained model sharing for scalable node-level anomaly detection.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Energy Management for Wearable IoT Devices with Conformal Prediction
problem: Energy management for battery-powered wearable IoT devices with stochastic ambient energy harvesting; existing point-prediction energy management methods do not account for prediction uncertainty.
method: Conformal prediction framework for future energy harvest that provides prediction intervals with provable coverage guarantees. Uncertainty regions are leveraged in a Monte Carlo sampling-based energy management algorithm that evaluates multiple decisions across sampled energy scenarios; results are aggregated via lightweight ML model to make near-optimal energy decisions.
